**Tier 4** — decisions — policies, overrides, scenarios · owned by `platform` · `public.plan_role_allowances`

**One row is** One project role's share of an organization's capacity pool: the percentage of the month's compute and of the series storage a member holding that role may use, and how many runs that member may have in flight. A row with no organization is the platform default; a row naming one overrides it for that organization alone.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `org_id` + `project_role` | UNIQUE constraint | `plan_role_allowances_org_role_key` |
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `plan_role_allowances_pkey` |

**Natural key:** `org_id` + `project_role` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `plan_role_allowances_org_role_key`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `super_admin` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | yes |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 1 — **1 with no predicate** |

The plan, not tenant data: readable by everyone (`plan_role_allowances_read`, `USING (true)`, select only) and written by no API role except through `admin_set_role_allowance`, which opens with `_assert_super_admin`, names the admin to the audit trigger (`app.current_user_id`) and closes with `log_admin_action`. The four defaults (owner 100 %, editor 60 %, analyst 25 %, viewer 0 % of compute and storage; 3 and 1 runs in flight for editor and analyst) are seeded by the migration. Read by `_capacity_state`, which both the admission check inside `create_simulation_run` and the Lab's `get_my_capacity` call, so the Run card and the dispatcher read one answer. The actor the share is resolved for is the app's asserted user (D28).

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 1 policy here grants access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `plan_role_allowances_read` — `SELECT` to `anon`, `authenticated`
>
> See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.
